affiliations.role_title: Naval intelligence and Pacific Fleet service before OSS assignment
affiliations.date_precision: The archival guide says Converse entered the Navy in 1941 and served in the Office of Naval Intelligence, the Pacific Fleet, and OSS, in that order; it supplies no transfer dates or rank.
affiliations.research_notes: The U.S. Navy is the best-supported immediate pre-OSS institutional affiliation. The source's ordered list supports a Navy-to-OSS pathway but does not establish whether ONI or the Pacific Fleet was the final specific command.

affiliations.organization_name_as_found: the staff of U.S. Senator Styles Bridges
affiliations.date_precision: The archival guide explicitly dates the Senate staff employment from 1937 to 1941, immediately before Converse entered the Navy in 1941.
affiliations.research_notes: This is the best-supported last civilian employer before wartime Navy service. The source does not give a narrower title, duties, pay status or employing committee.

affiliations.date_precision: The archival guide says Converse had earned a Bachelor of Arts in Economics and a law degree by 1934; it does not give matriculation or individual degree dates.
affiliations.research_notes: This is an educational affiliation, not an employer. The evidence does not establish Stanford employment.

affiliations.date_precision: The private-identifier-matched Army record dated 30 July 1945 carries civilian-occupation value 992; the visually inspected official NARA table defines 9-92 as Students.
affiliations.research_notes: The historical status category identifies no school, degree, employer, workplace or Army-to-OSS sequence. Because Army entry occurred late in the war, the category's temporal relation to OSS service is not assumed.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Edmund C Converse is a high-confidence match to the Stanford-trained Senate staff member who entered the Navy in 1941 and served in Naval Intelligence, the Pacific Fleet, and OSS.
claims.evidence_excerpt: served in the Office of Naval Intelligence, the Pacific Fleet, and the Office of Strategic Services
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A University of Wyoming archival guide gives the rare name, birth and education context, dated Senate employment, Navy entry, ordered wartime assignments and explicit OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The rare exact first and surname, matching middle initial in the index, explicit OSS service and detailed institutional chronology support one exceptionally specific authoritative match.
claims.temporal_assessment: The archival biography dates civilian staff employment to 1937-1941, Navy entry to 1941 and then lists Naval Intelligence, Pacific Fleet and OSS service.
claims.match_notes: High confidence, not confirmation: the public source omits the middle initial and the personnel file has not been reviewed. No facts from the nineteenth-century banker of the same name are transferred.
